title: AI-assisted Unreal fan project: fixing an evolution scale pop before cutting the trailer
author: Inevitable-Try900
selftext:
I am working on Pokémon: The Free Souls, an unofficial fan-made action RPG in Unreal Engine. This is a 38-second trailer from the running development build, including staged preview sequences. I use AI assistance for code, production scripts, trailer copy and logo artwork; the gameplay shots themselves are captured engine footage, not generated video.



One useful lesson from this revision was that a plausible-looking implementation still needed frame-by-frame checking. Caterpie's evolution was grounded, but the interpolated silhouette swelled and then snapped smaller when the final Metapod appeared. The correction kept the morph endpoints in a consistent space instead of effectively applying the changing scale twice. A numeric check on this captured case put the old peak height at about 76.5 cm against a 58.6 cm target; the corrected peak was about 58.6 cm. Four focused Unreal evolution tests passed, with one expected fallback warning. That is a check of this subsystem, not a claim that the whole demo is finished.



The other visual problem was communication: a cinematic battle edit made Pikachu seem stationary and turn-based. This cut uses captured movement, dodging and attacks against the actual Charmander opponent, with a glimpse of the attack wheel. Capture used a fixed step, so I am not treating the trailer's frame rate as a performance benchmark.



The game will be completely free, with no payment required to play. A short demo is in development, with no announced release date. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Pokémon rights holders. There is no development fundraiser or paid access being offered here.



The trailer is also on our project accounts:

Instagram: [https://www.instagram.com/departmentofdoingnothing/reel/DesLq5BsbRb/](https://www.instagram.com/departmentofdoingnothing/reel/DesLq5BsbRb/)

TikTok: [https://www.tiktok.com/@doingnothingdept/video/7698490148702424341](https://www.tiktok.com/@doingnothingdept/video/7698490148702424341)



For people using AI on animation or presentation code: which invariants do you test automatically, and which still need visual inspection? The scale check was useful here, but it would not have told us whether the evolution actually felt grounded.
